title: Nepal Bhutan and Sikkim Tour Package
highlights: Explore the scenic beauty and spirituality of Nepal, Bhutan, and Sikkim—where ancient monasteries, Himalayan peaks, and vibrant cultures create a one-of-a-kind journey.
Witness the devotion at Pashupatinath Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famed for its religious significance, ornate woodwork, and vibrant cultural atmosphere.
Experience the beauty of Tsomgo Lake, nestled in Sikkim’s mountains, celebrated for its crystal-clear waters, changing shades, and spiritual significance.
Visit Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park, Asia’s largest high-altitude zoo, famous for protecting rare species and offering close-up Himalayan wildlife experiences.
Discover Tiger’s Nest Monastery, Bhutan’s iconic cliffside temple perched 3,120 meters high, where Guru Rinpoche meditated.
overview: Embark on an incredible Nepal Bhutan Sikkim package tour that begins in Kathmandu, where you explore iconic sites like Boudhanath, Pashupatinath, and Durbar Square. Fly to Paro and visit the majestic Rinpung Dzong and Nyamai Zam. Trek to the iconic Tiger’s Nest Monastery, followed by a scenic drive to Thimphu for sights like the Memorial Chorten and Tashichho Dzong. Continue to Punakha to see its famed Dzong, Chimi Lhakhang, and Dochula Pass. Head to Phuentsholing to explore Bhutan Gate and Zangto Pelri. Cross into Kalimpong and visit Zang Dok Palri Monastery and vibrant markets. In Gangtok, admire Tsomgo Lake and Baba Harbhajan Singh Temple. Finally, relax in Darjeeling with visits to Batasia Loop, Ghoom Monastery, and the Himalayan Zoo before flying home.

know_before_you_go: Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
Images are for representation purposes only.
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

In cases of force majeure events (e.g., natural disasters, political unrest, or other unforeseeable circumstances), [Thrillophilia] reserves the right to reschedule tours & treks or offer alternative itineraries to ensure the safety and well-being of clients and staff.
Please note that prices are dynamic and may change in the peak season and on blackout dates.
Any breakage or damage of any items in the stay property will be charged at actuals.
Please note that the timings and duration of pick-up and drop-off transfers may vary based on certain factors like traffic, weather conditions, natural calamities, etc.
Prices may fluctuate with any change in services/hotels. The difference in the cost shall be borne by the client in case of any amendment in the package due to an increase in the number of guests.

If in case any traveller wants to or decides to leave the trip in the middle, all the expenses from the point onwards will be borne by the traveller. Neither the operator nor Thrillophilia will be held responsible for such decisions or for any refund.
It is recommended that you purchase travel insurance. Please note that the travel insurance is not included in the package price.

ID proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.
Children below 5 years are exempt, while those aged 6 to 12 receive a 50% concession.
To obtain entry into Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Tuesdays are observed as 'Dry Day' in Bhutan, during which alcohol consumption is avoided. Visitors are advised to respect this practice.
Travel Permit required for Indians beyond Paro and Thimphu. Your guide will arrange this.
Travellers aren't expected to wear the traditional kira, but you should make sure your clothing covers your arms and legs when entering any religious sites in Nepal, Bhutan and Sikkim.
Indian citizens need a valid passport or voter ID to enter Nepal and Bhutan.
Indian nationals can freely enter Sikkim but need special permits (PAP) for protected areas like Nathula Pass, Tsomgo Lake, and Yumthang Valley.
Protected Area Permits(PAP) is mandatory for Indians visiting restricted areas. It can be arranged easily through registered tour operators or travel agencies.
Foreign nationals must get a Restricted Area Permit (RAP), valid for 30 days (extendable to 60). It’s required even to enter Sikkim.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Kathmandu | Day at Leisure
days.desc: Welcome to Kathmandu! Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, get driven to your hotel. Check in and spend your time at leisure. You can visit Swayambhunath Stupa, perched atop a hill with breathtaking views and its iconic white dome crowned by golden spires—also called the Monkey Temple. You can also visit Narayanhiti Palace, the former royal residence, where traditional Nepalese design meets modern architecture, offering a glimpse into Nepal’s royal history and culture.

days.title: Full-Day Sightseeing in Kathmandu
days.desc: Today, get driven to Boudhanath Stupa, one of the largest spherical stupas in Nepal, known for its peaceful atmosphere and colorful prayer flags. Next, explore Kathmandu Durbar Square, a UNESCO World Heritage site filled with ancient palaces, temples, and vibrant local life. Later, visit Pashupatinath Temple, a sacred Hindu shrine on the Bagmati River, famous for its stunning architecture and spiritual rituals, offering a deep dive into Nepal’s rich cultural heritage.

days.title: Hike to Tiger's Nest Monastery
days.desc: Start your day with a scenic drive to Satsam Chencho Tshongkhang, the gateway to the iconic Tiger’s Nest Trek. Follow a forested trail lined with prayer flags as you ascend toward Taktsang Monastery, dramatically perched on a cliff at 3,000 meters. Known for its deep spiritual significance, this sacred site is believed to be where Guru Rinpoche meditated. Explore its ancient murals and meditation caves surrounded by breathtaking views. Afterward, hike back down and get driven to your hotel.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Post check-out, get driven to Thimphu. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and rest. Later, visit the National Memorial Chorten, where locals gather for daily prayers seeking blessings. Next, explore the National Library, home to rare Buddhist manuscripts. Step into the Folk Heritage Museum to experience authentic Bhutanese village life, then explore Tashichho Dzong, the seat of Bhutan’s government and summer home of the monastic body. Perfect for your Nepal Bhutan Sikkim Package Tour.

days.title: Excursion to Punakha
days.desc: Today, get driven to Punakha. Start your tour at Punakha Dzong, marveling at its stunning architecture & learning about its role as the winter home of Bhutan’s Je Khenpo. Next, visit Chimi Lhakhang, the Fertility Temple, where couples seek blessings for children. Then, walk across Punakha Suspension Bridge, the longest in Bhutan, and enjoy sweeping views of the Po Chhu River. Conclude at Dochula Pass, soaking in the serene atmosphere among 108 chortens with breathtaking Himalayan mountain views.

days.title: Transfer to Phuentsholing | Phuentsholing Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Post check out, get transferred to Phuentsholing. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and rest. Later, get driven to Bhutan Gate, the gateway symbolizing friendship between India and Bhutan. Next, explore the peaceful Karbandi Monastery, admired for its intricate murals and serene atmosphere. Stroll through the lively Phuentsholing Market, where authentic local goods bring the culture to life. Afterward, visit Zangto Pelri, a sacred temple modeled after Guru Rinpoche’s heavenly abode.

days.title: Transfer to Darjeeling | Day at Leisure
days.desc: In the morning, check out and get driven to Darjeeling. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and spend your time at leisure. You can explore Rock Garden, known for its terraced gardens, waterfalls, and peaceful surroundings nestled among the hills. You can visit Nightingale Park, a beautifully maintained garden offering panoramic views of the mountains, musical fountains, and a statue of Lord Shiva—making it a perfect spot to relax and soak in Darjeeling’s beauty. Afterward, return to your hotel.

days.title: Darjeeling Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, get driven to explore the city. Visit Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park, home to rare Himalayan species like the red panda and snow leopard. Next, visit Batasia Loop, a unique spiral railway track offering stunning views of the Himalayas. Continue to Ghoom Monastery, one of the oldest Tibetan monasteries in Darjeeling, known for its 15-foot Maitreya Buddha statue. Conclude at the Japanese Peace Pagoda, a symbol of harmony offering serene views and spiritual calm.
